answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that grows slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. Like a crystal forming layer by layer, an agent's standing should accumulate only through verified work over time, so creating a hundred fresh identities buys nothing. A shared lagoon of attestations lets honest peers vouch for each other, while a willow-like trust graph bends under pressure instead of snapping: suspicious clusters lose weight gradually rather than being banned outright, so attackers gain little from flooding the system with fake agents.
